subject: MidCity Bank - model evals & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@midcitybank.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@midcitybank.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MidCity Bank - model evals & next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the evaluation on Redwood: 

Summary of fit
- Goal: automated customer support triage + suggested responses for Tier 1 banking inquiries (account access, transfers, card disputes).
- Key constraints: PCI tokenization on PII, max latency 300ms p99 for single-turn queries, strict low-hallucination requirement for compliance.

Recommended starting model(s)
- Redwood-13B-v2 (quantized q4f) — good latency/cost balance, strong instruction-following in our benchmarks.
- Mistral-7B-instruct — lower cost for high-throughput routes; we recommend running side-by-side.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (8-bit) — alternative if you want a wider prompt-context evaluation.

Evaluation plan (high level)
- Run a 5k-sample eval (mix of prompts from live logs + synthetic edge cases).
- Metrics: exact-match on critical fields, hallucination rate (manual adjudication on a sampled subset), safety/PII leakage checks, token-cost per query, p50/p95 latency.
- Deliverables: benchmark report + recommended model and quantization profile; prompts and failure samples.

What we need from you
1) Dataset sample: CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_response, category, severity (see attached sample).
2) Confirm the scoring priority (example: 60% accuracy on critical fields, 20% hallucination, 20% latency/cost).
3) Any additional compliance checks (PCI/PHI notes) and preferred audit controls.

I've attached a sample CSV and an eval plan stub to make the upload smoother. Dylan and Dev are looped in to pick this up on the engineering side — Dylan will advise on prompts/metrics, Dev will run the eval and share the run config.

Next steps
- Priya/Tom: send dataset link (Drive or S3) + any scoring rubric by EOD Tue (04/13).
- Dylan/Dev: we'll schedule the first run once we have the data (aiming for a 48-hour turnaround).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: midcity-eval-dataset-sample.csv (sample), midcity-eval-plan.md (plan stub)

From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@midcitybank.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@midcitybank.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MidCity Bank - model evals & next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Dataset format: our analytics team can export a sample, but it currently contains columns for customer_id (tokenized), timestamp, user_message, agent_response, and outcome_code. Is that okay, or do you prefer an id/prompt/expected layout?
- Scoring: compliance wants a clear definition of hallucination. Can you propose a simple rubric we can use for the manual adjudication sample?
- Timing: Priya is concerned about PII in the training prompts; can Redwood handle a fully tokenized dataset (no raw PII) or do you need mappings?

Appreciate your help — we want to keep this scoped to a single vertical (card/disputes) for the first run.

—Tom
Senior Product Manager
MidCity Bank

On Sat, Apr 10, 2027 at 3:12 PM Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the evaluation on Redwood: ...

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@midcitybank.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MidCity Bank - model evals & next steps

Tom — good questions. Short answers first, details below.

1) Dataset layout: tokenized customer_id is fine. For the eval runner we need a CSV/JSONL with these canonical fields: id, prompt, expected_response, metadata. If you can provide a CSV with your existing columns, we can map them on upload (we'll share a mapping template).

2) Hallucination rubric (suggested)
- 0 = Correct: expected_response matches model output for critical fields (e.g., account number, transaction id)
- 1 = Minor deviation: paraphrase acceptable, meaning preserved, no missing critical facts
- 2 = Hallucination: model asserts unsupported facts or invents specifics (require manual review)
- 3 = Safety/PII leakage: returns any raw PII (fail automatically)

We'll run an automated extractor to flag likely hallucinations and then sample 200 cases for manual adjudication against the rubric. For compliance we can provide the adjudication spreadsheet.

3) PII: tokenized IDs are fine. If you need, we can accept a mapping file in a separate encrypted S3 bucket so the eval runner can verify behavior without exposing raw PII. Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for any encrypted artifacts.

Execution notes
- Upload: Drive link (preferred for initial sample) or S3 (for larger exports). Please add marissa@redwood.ai and dev@redwood.ai with access.
- Size: 3k–5k samples recommended for a reliable signal on accuracy/hallucination; run smaller pilot (500) first if you want faster feedback.
- Scoring: we'll report accuracy, hallucination-rate, avg tokens per response, and cost estimate. Latency numbers are from the dedicated Redwoods cluster and we'll include p50/p95.

Links
- Eval run template: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1aBcMidCityEval
- Past benchmark report (sample): https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/sample-banking-eval-202702

I'll kick off the mapping once we have the sample.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
